editorial:
If you love Batman stories that actually make you feel something, this animated movie is a must. The story follows Batman as he faces a new vigilante called Red Hood, who is cleaning up Gotham with brutal efficiency but without Batman's no-kill rule. The twist? Red Hood is actually Jason Todd, the former Robin who died years ago. The movie does a great job balancing action with real emotion, and the voice acting is top notch. You get plenty of mystery, crime, and heartbreak as Batman struggles with guilt and loss.

The animation is smooth and the fight scenes are exciting without being over the top. The pacing keeps you hooked from start to finish, and the story never drags. On the downside, some side characters feel a little underused, and the ending might leave you wanting more. Still, this is one of the best Batman animated films ever made. If you are a fan of dark superhero stories, you should definitely watch it. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Batman confronts Red Hood at an abandoned building. Red Hood reveals he survived his death and was brought back to life by the Lazarus Pit, but he is angry that Batman never avenged him by killing the Joker. Red Hood gives Batman a gun and demands he choose between killing the Joker or letting Red Hood do it. Batman refuses to kill, and Red Hood detonates explosives, escaping. The movie ends with Batman visiting Jason's grave, showing he still cares deeply about his lost partner.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark superhero stories and Batman fans.
